Done
I found the root cause. Stopping here to report before making changes, because the diagnosis changes what the next slice should be.

What's broken
dotnet test is green (934 total, 919 passing, 15 skipped). The two failures are both in MYRESTAURANT_E2E=1:

Display_PairsAndShowsRotatingQrAcrossWindowBoundary — the QR never changes in 60 s (3 windows at 20 s)
Admin_RotatesJoinSecret_InFlightTokenDiesNextWindowWorks — same, waiting for the rotated secret's code
Everything before the WaitForJoinQrPathAsync call passed in both, including AssertShowingLiveJoinCode on the first code. So the display renders a correct, live code once and then never re-renders.

Root cause: the E2E harness never gets a Blazor circuit
RestaurantInstance.CreateProcess sets ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production and boots the build output (bin/<Config>/net10.0) with ASPNETCORE_CONTENTROOT pointed at the source directory.

In dotnet/aspnetcore release/10.0, WebHost.ConfigureWebDefaults reads the build-time static-web-assets manifest only in Development:

csharp
builder.ConfigureAppConfiguration((ctx, cb) =>
{
    if (ctx.HostingEnvironment.IsDevelopment())
    {
        StaticWebAssetsLoader.UseStaticWebAssets(ctx.HostingEnvironment, ctx.Configuration);
    }
});
_framework/blazor.web.js is a framework static web asset. dotnet publish copies it into wwwroot/_framework (which is why the container works, and why dev works — that's Development). A build output served as Production has neither: Program.cs only calls app.UseStaticFiles(), so GET /_framework/blazor.web.js → 404. No circuit. TableDisplay.razor is prerendered HTML only, and OnAfterRender — where the refresh loop starts — never runs at all.

That also means no E2E scenario has ever exercised an interactive surface; the five passing ones are all static-SSR, which is why this went unnoticed.

A second, real product bug behind it
Even with the circuit up, TableDisplay.razor has a live race:

csharp
protected override void OnAfterRender(bool firstRender)
{
    if (!firstRender || _stage is DisplayStage.NotPaired or DisplayStage.WrongTable) return;
    _subscription = Broadcaster.Subscribe(OnDomainNotification);
    _ = RunRefreshLoopAsync();
}
ComponentBase.RunInitAndSetParametersAsync calls StateHasChanged() as soon as OnInitializedAsync yields — and it yields on the first of four DB round trips inside LoadAsync. The client's acknowledgement of that first (empty) batch will usually beat those round trips, so OnAfterRender(firstRender: true) fires while _stage is still its default NotPaired. The guard returns, firstRender is never true again, and the loop never starts. A display frozen on the code it was born with — §11.5's stated worst failure — intermittently, in production. Separately, RunRefreshLoopAsync only catches OperationCanceledException/ObjectDisposedException, so one transient DB error kills the loop permanently and silently.

Verified against dotnet/aspnetcore release/10.0
StaticWebAssetsLoader.ResolveManifest returns null when <AppName>.staticwebassets.runtime.json is absent → calling it in a published deployment is a no-op, so the fix costs production nothing.
StaticWebAssetsLoader.UseStaticWebAssets(IWebHostEnvironment, IConfiguration) is public shipped API.
ComponentBase.RendererInfo → RendererInfo(Name, IsInteractive); RemoteRenderer = ("Server", true), Web.HtmlRendering.StaticHtmlRenderer = ("Static", false). Safe to read in BuildRenderTree.
ConfigureWebHostBuilder.ConfigureAppConfiguration does not throw (it runs eagerly and only rejects host-config key changes), but calling the loader after builder.Build() and before app.UseStaticFiles() is the predictable placement.
The slice I'd deliver next (say go and I'll produce the tar.gz)
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Program.cs — load the build-time manifest outside Development; no-op when published.
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Components/Pages/Display/TableDisplay.razor — start the live work idempotently, gated on RendererInfo.IsInteractive instead of firstRender; make the refresh loop survive a transient failure; publish data-live so a dead circuit is observable.
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Displays/DisplayRefreshSchedule.cs (new) — the boundary arithmetic pulled out of Razor, with the ceiling no longer truncating a legitimate full-window wait.
tests/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tests/Displays/DisplayRefreshScheduleTests.cs (new) — fast unit coverage for it.
tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/Harness/RestaurantInstance.cs — probe /_framework/blazor.web.js during readiness and refuse to start with a message naming the cause.
tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/Harness/DisplayJourneys.cs + EndToEndScenarios.cs — wait for data-live before watching the QR, so this can never again fail as an unexplained timeout.
docs/_append/BUILD_PROGRESS-m6-slice-4.md, _CHANGES.md.
Files to delete: none. No migration, no schema change, no package change.

One thing worth your judgement before I write it: I'm fixing this in Program.cs rather than flipping the harness to Development, because "build output + ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production" is a combination a real operator will try and losing all interactivity silently is a bad trap. If you'd rather keep product code untouched and have the harness publish instead, that's a bigger but arguably purer change — tell me which you want.
